vsm2.22:1.1:
I. Change-of-lineage, paths, and fruits Change-of-lineage knowledge comes next. Its position is to advert to the path, so it belongs
neither to purification by knowledge and vision of the way nor of knowledge and vision, but is intermediate, unassignable.
vsm2.22:1.2: Still it is reckoned as insight because it falls in line with insight.
vsm2.22:2.1:
Purification by knowledge and vision properly consists in knowledge of the four paths —
stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and Arahantship.
vsm2.22:3.1: Herein, nothing further needs to be done by one who wants to achieve, firstly, the knowledge of the first path.
vsm2.22:3.2: For what he needs to do has already been done by arousing the insight that ends in conformity knowledge.
vsm2.22:4.1:
As soon as conformity knowledge has arisen thus, and the murk hiding the truths is dispelled by the force peculiar to each
of the three conformities, his mind no longer enters, settles, resolves, clings, cleaves or clutches on any field of formations.
vsm2.22:4.2: It retreats, retracts and recoils, as water does from a lotus leaf.
vsm2.22:4.3: Every sign as object, every occurrence as object, appears as an impediment.
vsm2.22:5.1: Then, while every sign and occurrence appears as an impediment, when conformity knowledge’s repetition has ended,
vsm2.22:5.2: change-of-lineage knowledge arises, which takes as its object the signless, non-occurrence, non-formation, cessation, Nibbāna,
vsm2.22:5.3:
which passes out of the lineage, category and plane of the ordinary man and enters
the lineage, category and plane of the Noble Ones,
vsm2.22:5.4: which, being the first adverting, the first concern, the first reaction, to Nibbāna as object,
vsm2.22:5.5:
fulfils the state of a condition for the path in six ways — proximity, contiguity,
repetition, decisive-support, absence, and disappearance,
vsm2.22:5.6: which is the culminating peak of insight, and which is irrevocable — thus arises change-of-lineage knowledge.
vsm2.22:5.7:
Of which it is said: ‘How is understanding of emergence and turning away from the external
change-of-lineage knowledge? It overcomes arising, thus it is change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:5.8:
It overcomes occurrence … and so on through … despair, thus it is change-of-lineage.
It overcomes the sign of formations externally, thus it is change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:5.9:
It enters into non-arising, thus it is change-of-lineage … and so on … it
enters into cessation, Nibbāna, thus it is change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:5.10:
Having overcome arising, it enters into non-arising, thus it is change-of-lineage’
(Paṭis I 56) — and so on, all to be quoted in full.’
vsm2.22:6.1:
Here is a simile illustrating how conformity and change-of-lineage occur with different objects,
though occurring in a single cognitive series with a single adverting.
vsm2.22:6.2:
Suppose a man wanted to leap across a broad stream and establish himself on the far bank:
he runs fast and, seizing a rope or pole hanging from a branch on the near bank, leaps —
vsm2.22:6.3:
with his body tending toward the far bank; on arriving above it, he lets go,
falls onto the far bank staggering, then steadies himself there.
vsm2.22:6.4:
So too this meditator, wanting to establish himself on Nibbāna, the bank opposite becoming,
runs fast by contemplation of rise and fall, etc.,
vsm2.22:6.5:
and seizing, without letting go, the rope of materiality or a pole among feeling, etc.,
as impermanent, painful or not-self, by conformity’s adverting,
vsm2.22:6.6:
leaps with the first conformity consciousness, and with the second tends and inclines
toward Nibbāna, like the body inclining to the far bank;
vsm2.22:6.7:
with the third, like arriving above the far bank, he is near to the now-attainable
Nibbāna, and with that consciousness’s ceasing he lets go the formation as object,
vsm2.22:6.8: and with the change-of-lineage consciousness falls onto the unformed Nibbāna, the opposite bank.
vsm2.22:6.9:
But, staggering for lack of repetition on a single object, like the man, he is not yet
properly steady; after that he is steadied by path knowledge.
vsm2.22:7.1: Herein, conformity is able to dispel the murk of defilements concealing the truths but unable to make Nibbāna its object.
vsm2.22:7.2: Change-of-lineage can only make Nibbāna its object, but cannot dispel the murk concealing the truths.
vsm2.22:8.1:
Here is a simile: a man with eyes went out at night to find the conjunction of the stars, and looked
up to see the moon, but it was invisible, concealed by clouds.
vsm2.22:8.2: Then a wind sprang up and blew away the thick clouds; another blew away the medium clouds; and another blew away the fine clouds.
vsm2.22:8.3: Then the man saw the moon in the cloudless sky, and found out the conjunction of the stars.
vsm2.22:9.1:
Herein, the three clouds are like the thick, medium and fine darkness concealing the truths; the three winds are like
the three conformity consciousnesses; the man with eyes is like change-of-lineage knowledge; the moon is like Nibbāna;
vsm2.22:9.2: the successive blowing away of clouds by each wind is like each conformity consciousness dispelling the murk concealing the truths;
vsm2.22:9.3:
the man’s seeing the clear moon in the cloudless sky is like change-of-lineage knowledge’s
seeing clear Nibbāna when the murk concealing the truths has disappeared.
vsm2.22:10.1:
Just as the three winds can only blow away the clouds concealing the moon but cannot see the moon,
so the three conformities can only dispel the murk concealing the truths but cannot see Nibbāna.
vsm2.22:10.2:
Just as the man can only see the moon but cannot blow away the clouds, so change-of-lineage
knowledge can only see Nibbāna but cannot dispel the defilements.
vsm2.22:10.3: Hence it is called “adverting to the path.”
vsm2.22:11.1:
For although it is not adverting, it occupies the position of adverting, and, as it
were giving a sign to the path to come into being, it ceases.
vsm2.22:11.2:
Without pausing after that sign, the path follows in uninterrupted continuity, and as it comes into being it
pierces and explodes the mass of greed, hate and delusion never pierced before.
vsm2.22:12.1:
Here is a simile: an archer had a target set up at a distance of eight usabhas, and, wrapping
his face in a cloth and arming himself with an arrow, stood on a revolving wheel-platform.
vsm2.22:12.2: Another man turned the wheel, and when the target faced the archer, he gave him a sign with a stick.
vsm2.22:12.3: Without pausing after the sign, the archer shot the arrow and hit the target.
vsm2.22:13.1: Herein, change-of-lineage knowledge is like the sign with the stick; path knowledge is like the archer.
vsm2.22:13.2:
Path knowledge’s making Nibbāna its object without pausing after change-of-lineage’s sign, and piercing the never-before-pierced
mass of greed, hate and delusion, is like the archer hitting the target without pausing after the sign.
vsm2.22:14.1:
Not only does it pierce this mass of greed, etc., but it also dries up the ocean of suffering of the beginningless
round of rebirths, closes all doors to the states of loss, provides actual experience of the seven
noble treasures, abandons the eightfold wrong path, and allays all enmity and fear,
vsm2.22:14.2:
leads to the state of the Fully Enlightened One’s breast-born son, and to the acquisition of many hundred other blessings — thus
the knowledge associated with the path of stream-entry, provider of many blessings, is called knowledge of the path of stream-entry.
vsm2.22:14.3: The first kind of knowledge is ended.
vsm2.22:15.1: Immediately next to that knowledge, however, there arise either two or three fruition consciousnesses, which are its result.
vsm2.22:15.2:
For it is owing to this very fact that supramundane profitable consciousness results immediately that it
is said, “And which he called the concentration with immediate result” (Sn 226), and “Sluggishly he reaches
what has immediate result for the destruction of the cankers” (A II 149), and so on.
vsm2.22:16.1: Some, however, say that there are one, two, three, four, or five fruition consciousnesses. That is inadmissible.
vsm2.22:16.2:
For change-of-lineage knowledge arises at the end of conformity’s repetition,
so at the minimum there must be two conformity consciousnesses,
vsm2.22:16.3:
since one alone does not act as repetition condition. And a single series of impulsions
has a maximum of seven impulsion consciousnesses.
vsm2.22:16.4:
Consequently, that series which has two conformities and change-of-lineage as a third and path
consciousness as fourth has three fruition consciousnesses.
vsm2.22:16.5: That which has three conformities and change-of-lineage as fourth and path consciousness as fifth has two fruition consciousnesses.
vsm2.22:16.6: That is why it was said above, “There arise either two or three fruition consciousnesses.”
vsm2.22:17.1:
Then some say that which has four conformities and change-of-lineage as fifth and path
consciousness as sixth has one fruition consciousness.
vsm2.22:17.2:
But that is refuted because it is the fourth or fifth impulsion that reaches the path,
not those after that, owing to their nearness to the life-continuum.
vsm2.22:17.3: So that cannot be accepted as correct.
vsm2.22:18.1: And at this point this stream-enterer is called the second noble person.
vsm2.22:18.2:
However negligent he may be, he is bound to make an end of suffering when he has travelled and traversed
the round of rebirths among deities and human beings for the seventh time.
vsm2.22:19.1:
At the end of the fruition his consciousness enters the life-continuum. After that, it arises as mind-door adverting interrupting
the life-continuum for the purpose of reviewing the path. When that has ceased, seven impulsions of path reviewing arise.
vsm2.22:19.2:
After re-entry into the life-continuum, adverting, etc., arise again in the same
way for the purpose of reviewing fruition, and so on.
vsm2.22:19.3:
With the arising of these he reviews the path, he reviews the fruition, he reviews the defilements
abandoned, he reviews the defilements still remaining, and he reviews Nibbāna.
vsm2.22:20.1: He reviews the path in this way, “So this is the path I have come by.”
vsm2.22:20.2: Next he reviews the fruition after that in this way, “This is the blessing I have obtained.”
vsm2.22:20.3: Next he reviews the defilements that have been abandoned, “These are the defilements abandoned in me.”
vsm2.22:20.4: Next he reviews the defilements still to be eliminated by the three higher paths, “These are the defilements still remaining in me.”
vsm2.22:20.5: And lastly he reviews the deathless Nibbāna in this way, “This is the state (dhamma) that has been penetrated by me as object.”
vsm2.22:20.6: So the noble disciple who is a stream-enterer has five kinds of reviewing.
vsm2.22:21.1: And as in the case of the stream-enterer, so also in the cases of the once-returner and non-returner.
vsm2.22:21.2: But the Arahant has no reviewing of remaining defilements. So all the kinds of reviewing total nineteen.
vsm2.22:21.4: Trainers may or may not have the reviewing of the defilements abandoned and those still remaining.
vsm2.22:21.5:
In fact it was owing to the absence of such reviewing that Mahānāma asked the Blessed One, “What state is there still unabandoned
by me internally owing to which at times states of greed invade my mind and remain?” (M I 91) all of which should be quoted.
vsm2.22:22.1:
However, after reviewing in this way, either while sitting in the same session or on another occasion, the noble disciple who
is a stream-enterer makes it his task to reach the second plane by attenuating both greed for sense desires and ill-will.
vsm2.22:22.2:
He brings to bear the faculties, the powers, and the enlightenment factors, and he works over and turns up that same
field of formations, classed as materiality, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, with the knowledge
that they are impermanent, painful, not-self, and he embarks upon the progressive series of insights.
vsm2.22:23.1:
When he has done so, and when, at the end of equanimity about formations, conformity and change-of-lineage knowledge
have arisen in a single adverting in the way already described, then the path of once-return arises next to change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:23.2: The knowledge associated with that is knowledge of the path of once-return.
vsm2.22:23.3: The second kind of knowledge is ended.
vsm2.22:24.1:
The Second Fruition—Fourth Noble Person The fruition consciousness should be understood to follow
immediately upon this knowledge in the same way as before.
vsm2.22:24.2:
And at this point this once-returner is called the fourth noble person.
He is bound to make an end of suffering after returning once to this world.
vsm2.22:24.3: Next there comes reviewing in the way already described.
vsm2.22:25.1:
Now, after reviewing in this way, either while sitting in the same session or on another occasion,
this noble disciple who is a once-returner makes it his task to reach the third plane by abandoning,
without remainder, both greed for the sense desires and ill-will.
vsm2.22:25.2:
He brings to bear the faculties, the powers, and the enlightenment factors, and he works over and turns up that same field of
formations with the knowledge that they are impermanent, painful, not-self, and he embarks upon the progressive series of insights.
vsm2.22:26.1:
When he has done so, and when, at the end of equanimity about formations, conformity and change-of-lineage have arisen in a single
adverting in the way already described, then the path of non-return arises next to change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:26.2: The knowledge associated with that is knowledge of the path of non-return.
vsm2.22:26.3: The third kind of knowledge is ended.
vsm2.22:27.1:
The Third Fruition—Sixth Noble Person The fruition consciousnesses should be understood to follow
immediately upon this knowledge in the same way as before.
vsm2.22:27.2:
And at this point this non-returner is called the sixth noble person. After death he reappears apparitionally elsewhere and attains
complete extinction there without ever returning, without ever coming to this world again through rebirth-linking.
vsm2.22:27.3: Next there comes reviewing in the way already described.
vsm2.22:28.1:
Now, after reviewing in this way, either while sitting in the same session or on another occasion,
this noble disciple who is a non-returner makes it his task to reach the fourth plane by abandoning,
without remainder, greed for the fine-material and immaterial, conceit (pride), agitation, and ignorance.
vsm2.22:28.2:
He brings to bear the faculties, the powers, and the enlightenment factors, and he works over and turns up that same field of
formations with the knowledge that they are impermanent, painful, not-self, and he embarks upon the progressive series of insights.
vsm2.22:29.1:
When he has done so, and when, at the end of equanimity about formations, conformity and change-of-lineage
have arisen in a single adverting, then the path of Arahantship arises next to change-of-lineage.
vsm2.22:29.2: The knowledge associated with that is knowledge of the path of Arahantship.
vsm2.22:29.3: The fourth kind of knowledge is ended.
